1. Summary of the primary business
We are a technology platform, built on proprietary digital technology and pan-India digital connectivity as the 
foundational layer driving digital transformation in India. Since our inception, we have played a pivotal role in 
democratising access to digital connectivity and digital services in India. Jio Platforms’ digital connectivity forms one 
of the fundamental pillars of India’s growing digital economy which is expected to reach $1.4 trillion (₹125.8 trillion) 
by Fiscal 2031, as per the Analysys Mason Report. Our Subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (“RJIL”) served 
533.3 million customers in India1
as of June 30, 2026. A combination of mobile, fixed broadband and digital services 
across a unified platform, together with data and customer personalisation, positions us as a comprehensive digital 
gateway through which a significant proportion of Indian customers are able to access the internet, digital services and 
emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (“AI”). 
Our Technology Platform 
In modern software-driven network architecture, the traditional distinction between ‘telecom’ and ‘technology’ no longer 
applies. Our position is more grounded in technology, given that we have designed, built, and deployed our entire 
network and services stack primarily using proprietary technology, from radio access network to core capabilities, from 
operating systems to digital applications. Technology is the fundamental architecture of how our business is structured, 
built, and operated. 
In this context:
a) Our Company had 12,477 full-time employees in digital products and technology development as of June 30, 2026, 
representing approximately 45% of our total full-time employees. Of these 12,477 employees, 8,156 are involved 
in the development of digital products and services while the remaining are engaged in network technology 
engineering; 
b) We have filed 7,220 patent applications across 4G, 5G, 6G cloud-native core network architectures, AI-driven 
network automation, and digital technologies - with 2,655 applications in India and 4,565 filed across foreign 
jurisdictions, as of June 30, 2026. We are the only Indian company to be among the top 20 companies globally in 
the WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty rankings in 20252
- a distinction that places us alongside leading global 
technology firms;

a. Business Overview - Products and Services
Our offerings encompass various aspects of modern digital society, as described below: 
We offer consumers:
• Digital Connectivity (4G, 5G, JioFiber, JioAirFiber): Mobile and fixed broadband services provided by RJIL to 
subscribers as per their connectivity plans; 
• Digital Entertainment (JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioGames, JioHotstar): Video/music streaming and cloud gaming 
provided by the Company, RJIL and Saavn Media Limited bundled with connectivity plans;
• Cloud and Productivity (JioAICloud, JioPC): Cloud storage and virtual PC services provided by the Company to 
subscribers on bundled or standalone basis;
• Smart Home and IoT (Jio Set-top-box, JioHome): Connected devices enabling home automation. “IoT” (Internet 
of Things) refers to a network of connected devices and sensors that collect, exchange and act on data with minimal 
human intervention. Provided by the Company and RJIL on device sale or subscription basis; and
• AI Products (JioBrain, Google AI Pro): AI assistants and personalised digital experiences provided by the 
Company and Jio Haptik Technologies Limited in partnership with third parties and offered as bundled with the 
connectivity plans. 
We offer businesses:
• Enterprise Connectivity (JioBusiness, Internet Leased Line (“ILL”)4
, MPLS5 VPN6
): Broadband and leased line 
connectivity provided by RJIL on a contract-based subscription model;

Enterprise cloud, Wi-Fi, and security solutions provided by the Company and RJIL in partnership with Microsoft 
and Google Cloud on subscription basis;
• Managed Services (Managed Network Operations Centre (“NoC”), unified communications): End-to-end

• Enterprise AI (JioBrain): AI enterprise suite for forecasting, automation and network optimisation provided by the 
Company on subscription/ usage basis.

b. Industries Served and Typical Customers
We serve in the digital connectivity and digital services industry. Our Material Subsidiary, RJIL, served 533.3 million 
customers in India, as of June 30, 2026.
c. Segment Reporting and Revenue Contribution
Since our Company is mainly engaged in the business of digital services platform, application and software business, 
it operates in a single segment as per the requirements of Ind AS 108 – Operating Segments. For further information, 
see “Restated Consolidated Financial Information – Note: 43 – Segment Reporting” on page 428 of the Red Herring 
Prospectus.
d. Key Geographies Served
Majority of our operations are in India, which constituted 96.62% of our Revenue from Operations in Fiscal 2026. 
e. Revenue Concentration Among Top 5 Customers
We are engaged in the business of providing digital services and digital connectivity. Our Material Subsidiary, RJIL, 
contributed 87.34% and 87.74% of the Company’s consolidated Revenue from Operations in the three months ended 
June 30, 2026 and Fiscal 2026, respectively. RJIL served 533.3 million customers as of June 30, 2026, including 
mobile broadband and fixed broadband customers. There is no concentration of revenue amongst our customers given 
the scale of operations and the extremely large customer base of RJIL.
f. Key Facilities
Our Registered Office is located at Office – 101, Saffron, Nr. Centre Point, Panchwati 5 Rasta, Ambawadi, Ahmedabad 
380 006, Gujarat India, and our Corporate Office is located at TC-22, 5th Floor, A wing, Reliance Corporate Park, 
Thane Belapur Road, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai 400 701, Maharashtra India. 
g. Business Strengths and Strategies
Our Strengths
(i) A technology company with inherent engineering and full-stack proprietary capabilities.
a) Our platform is built on a vertically integrated proprietary technology stack and core capabilities across 
network, device engineering, software and operating systems and applications;

at nationwide scale - including a 4G+5G combination core, 5G devices and OSS and BSS operating systems,

Analysys Mason Report.
(ii) Transforming digital connectivity and digital services in India.
a) We were the first to roll out 4G VoLTE connectivity at scale in India and the first company to achieve 100 
million 4G customers in less than 180 days from commercial launch of our services, as per the Analysys 
Mason Report;
b) We are the first operator in India to launch a standalone 5G network and have also enabled large scale, rapid

c) We had a 61.73% share of net fixed broadband customer additions in the three months ended June 30, 2026, 
as per the Analysys Mason Report;
d) In the three months ended June 30, 2026, we had 78.62% market share in 5G or UBR-based FWA, as per 
the Analysys Mason Report;
e) In the three months ended June 30, 2026, we provided 333.6 million OTT and music streaming subscription 
offers to customers, monthly, integrated with digital connectivity plans;
f) As of June 30, 2026, 28.6 million customers subscribe to our JioFiber or JioAirFiber services, making us 
the largest fixed broadband service provider in India, as per the Analysys Mason Report; and
g) As per the Analysys Mason Report, RJIL through JioAirFiber has the largest FWA based fixed broadband 
customer base in India as of June 30, 2026.
(iii) Culture of innovation driving execution engine excellence.
a) JioGridX: Records network data across 82 parameters at a given location across speed, coverage and user 
traffic, enabling automated and real-time improvement actions for seamless work orders to field teams and 
network operations centre;
b) Digital twin technology: Created a digital replica of network infrastructure including towers, equipment, 
fibre infrastructure, and buildings to assess network coverage in real-time, plan network rollouts and 
remotely guide field-engineers for first-time right installation;
c) Decentralised ‘fractal’ operations model: Pan-India operations divided into clusters serviced by Jio Centres 
covering multiple Jio Points across rural and urban markets, enabling simultaneous rollouts with minimal 
operational bottlenecks and reduced time-to-market;
d) JioBrain AI platform: Proprietary AI engine embedded across network operations enabling autonomous 
decision-making for capacity allocation, fault prediction and resolution, and real-time network optimisation;

a) As per the Analysys Mason Report, our pan-India reach, large and highly engaged customer base, together

cloud compute (including JioPC), cloud gaming and smart home solutions; and

and JioAirFiber packages.

a) Our network infrastructure is built on technological elements that we have pioneered;
b) As of June 30, 2026, we had access to a pan-India network of 360,537 Network Towers, majority of which 
are fiberised;
c) In Fiscal 2026, ~60% of India’s wireless data traffic was on our network, and as of June 30, 2026, we were 
the largest digital connectivity player, with ~1.4 times the 4G+5G subscribers of the second largest player 
in India, as per the Analysys Mason Report;
d) As of June 30, 2026, our wireless broadband network covered more than 99% of the population, while our 
fixed broadband coverage extended to cover approximately 98% of all pin codes in India;
e) We held 26,800.8 MHz spectrum, with average remaining life of approximately 15.8 years as of June 30, 
2026;
f) We have access to over 1.0 million route kilometres (or 30.0 million+ fibre pair kilometres of which more 
than 60% is intracity) of fibre network as per the Analysys Mason Report; and
g) We are the only operator in India to have spectrum in low-band, mid-band and millimetre wave (700 MHz, 
3300 MHz and 26GHz) spectrum for 5G, as per the Analysys Mason Report.
(vi) Proven track record of scale, growth and profitability with strong balance sheet.
a) In the three months ended June 30, 2026 and Fiscal 2026, we generated total revenue from operations of 
₹391,729 million and ₹1,468,853 million, EBITDA of ₹208,645 million and ₹762,554 million, and EBITDA 
margin of 53.26% and 51.91%, respectively;

b) We achieved this scale in just 10 years since the launch of digital connectivity services by RJIL in 2016;
c) Our revenue from operations and EBITDA grew at a compound annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of 15.79% 
and 17.79%, respectively, between Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2026. Further, between the three months ended 
June 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026, our revenue from operations and EBITDA increased 11.82% and 15.05% 
respectively;
d) We have a strong balance sheet which is reflected in our improving leverage position – our Net Leverage 
reduced from 0.88x in Fiscal 2024 to 0.36x in Fiscal 2026;
e) Our PAT was ₹77,641 million and ₹300,491 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and Fiscal 
2026 respectively and our PAT margin was 19.82% and 20.46% in the three months ended June 30, 2026 
and Fiscal 2026, respectively; and

(55.17%) and ₹166,807 million (79.95%) in Fiscal 2026 and the three months ended June 30, 2026, 
respectively.
Our Growth Strategies
(i) Continue to add new mobility consumers and extend our market leadership.
a) 261.0 million Indians users remain on 2G networks as of June 30, 2026, as per the Analysys Mason Report, 
there is a large addressable opportunity for their migration to 4G and 5G networks; and
b) JioBharat phone, priced at ₹799 bundled with affordable mobility plans, delivers smartphone-equivalent 
utility on an entry-level device to convert voice-only 2G users into active data consumers.
(ii) Continue transforming digital connectivity and digital services at home.
a) Fixed broadband penetration in India is only ~21% compared to developed and developing economies as 
of March 31, 2026, and is expected to increase to ~46% by Fiscal 2031 with 150.4 million customers, as 
per the Analysys Mason Report; and
b) Captured 61.73% of the market share in net fixed broadband customer additions in the three months ended 
June 30, 2026, with JioAirFiber scaling to 14.0 million customers as of June 30, 2026, as per the Analysys 
Mason Report.
(iii) Expand and deepen our business customer base.
a) Our managed services stack for business, delivers vertically integrated digital solutions such as
infrastructure, digital connectivity, cloud, digital services and cyber security, enabling an outcome-oriented 
managed services with end-to-end responsibility for delivering outcomes to business customers, which can 
create deeper engagement and higher value per customer relationship; and
b) Micro, small and medium enterprises (“MSME”) segment is significantly underpenetrated in India with 
enterprise digital services adoption estimated at less than 3.0%, representing a growth opportunity over 79 
million MSMEs, as per the Analysys Mason Report.
(iv) Monetise our platforms in overseas markets.
a) Proprietary technology stack including cloud-native radio access network (“RAN”), 5G core, OSS/BSS 
platforms, UBR-based FWA solutions, and AI-driven network automation and digital services platform has 
global applicability for network upgrades, 5G rollout and FWA-led broadband expansion; and
b) We believe our demonstrated ability to efficiently build and operate large-scale networks in India positions 
us to meaningfully expand globally.
(v) Leverage AI to build and deploy autonomous platforms across digital connectivity and other enterprise verticals.

a) JioBrain AI engine embedded across network operations enables autonomous decision-making for capacity 
allocation, fault prediction and resolution, and real-time network optimisation; and
b) AI capabilities built through customer, network and operational insights from serving over 533.3 million 
customers, as of June 30, 2026, intended to be extended to other global telecom companies and industry
verticals.

h. Listed Industry Peers

the fastest adopters of 5G globally, with ~43% of mobile broadband customers transitioning within less than 4 years as

growth to one of rapid acceleration. However, India continues to lag behind both developing and developed markets on 
fixed broadband penetration, implying significant room for future growth. There is also significant disparity between 
fixed broadband penetration in urban and rural areas in India. As digital connectivity providers overcome these barriers 
around limited network availability through next-generation technologies like FWA on 5G and UBR9
